# Notes -- #5079 "Conflict with DirectX-Headers"

batch-019. Ground truth: `main-debug`, public upstream commit
`89e2f98e29c289ae8ad9e00dd310104fea9fd7df` (verified via `dxc --version` and a
tree-diff control against upstream -- see method-notes.md).

## Summary

The reporter is right, and the defect is still present today. It is not a
`dxc.exe`/HLSL bug: two independent projects, DXC and DirectX-Headers, each
ship their own from-scratch, independently-authored shim that defines the
same set of Windows base types for non-Windows targets (`BYTE`, `BOOLEAN`,
`BOOL`, `LONG`, `ULONG`, `LONGLONG`, `LONG_PTR`, `ULONG_PTR`, `ULONGLONG`,
`_GUID`/`GUID`, `REFGUID`, `REFCLSID`, ...), with disagreeing underlying
types for several of them. Combining both in one translation unit -- which
is exactly what the reporter's Linux build does by consuming both DXC's
public `dxc/dxcapi.h` and DirectX-Headers -- is a hard `clang`
"typedef redefinition with different types" / "redefinition of '_GUID'"
compile error. There is no dxc.exe/HLSL angle to bisect: every stable DXC
release ships the same from-scratch `WinAdapter.h` design, and the conflict
is entirely with a different project's headers.

## Why `dxc.exe` is not the instrument

`cmd.txt`/`match.json` (dxc-driven, `.hlsl`-file probes) do not apply here:
there is no `.hlsl` input, and the reported failure is a C++ preprocessor/
header conflict, not a shader-compilation result. `expected.md` records the
"reproduces"/"does not reproduce" predicate for this non-dxc case; `clang`
is the instrument, and every probe is captured under `manual-case-*.txt`
per the skill's convention (command + exit code header, generated by
`gen-manual-case.py`, never hand-transcribed).

## Faithful local repro, not an approximation

This repository's own two vendored header trees already contain the exact
same-named, differently-typed shims the reporter hit -- no external fetch
was needed:

- `include/dxc/WinAdapter.h` -- DXC's own non-Windows shim, only pulled in
  by `dxc/dxcapi.h` when `_WIN32` is undefined (confirmed by reading
  `dxc/dxcapi.h` lines 13-38).
- `external/DirectX-Headers/include/wsl/winadapter.h` -- the pinned
  DirectX-Headers submodule's own non-Windows shim, defining the identical
  set of type names (`BYTE`, `BOOLEAN`, `BOOL`, `LONG`, `ULONG`, `LONGLONG`,
  `LONG_PTR`, `ULONG_PTR`, `ULONGLONG`, `GUID`/`_GUID`, `REFGUID`,
  `REFCLSID`).

`repro.cpp` (`#include <wsl/winadapter.h>` then `#include <dxc/dxcapi.h>`,
compiled with `_WIN32` undefined -- see `gen-manual-case.py`) reproduces the
exact class of error, naming the exact symbols, with the exact underlying-
type mismatches the PR #8431 author independently found (see below):

```
include/dxc/WinAdapter.h:303:14: error: typedef redefinition with different types ('BYTE' (aka 'unsigned char') vs 'char')
include/dxc/WinAdapter.h:306:14: error: typedef redefinition with different types ('bool' vs 'uint32_t' (aka 'unsigned int'))
include/dxc/WinAdapter.h:310:14: error: typedef redefinition with different types ('long' vs 'int32_t' (aka 'int'))
include/dxc/WinAdapter.h:312:23: error: typedef redefinition with different types ('unsigned long' vs 'uint32_t' (aka 'unsigned int'))
include/dxc/WinAdapter.h:376:16: error: redefinition of '_GUID'
...
include/dxc/WinAdapter.h:486:3: error: typedef redefinition with different types ('struct tagSTATSTG' vs 'STATSTG')
```

Full capture: `manual-case-clang-conflict.txt` (exit 1). Note line 303's
`BYTE` mismatch is `'unsigned char' vs 'char'` -- this is `BOOLEAN`'s
underlying type at that point in the file (the two shims define `BOOLEAN`
in terms of `BYTE`/`char` respectively before `BYTE` itself is even
compared), matching the reporter's own transcript, which shows the same
`BOOLEAN`/`BYTE`/`BOOL`/`LONG`/`ULONG`/`_GUID` symbol set.

### Controls

- `control-dxc-only.cpp` -- DXC's `dxc/dxcapi.h` alone, no DirectX-Headers
  in the TU. Compiles clean (exit 0; only harmless
  `-Wmacro-redefined` warnings for SAL/`_countof` macros that are already
  visible from the real Windows SDK headers on this build host -- unrelated
  to the reported defect, since these are warnings, not the redefinition
  *errors* the issue is about). Capture:
  `manual-case-clang-control-dxc-only.txt`.
- `control-directx-headers-only.cpp` -- DirectX-Headers' `wsl/winadapter.h`
  alone, no DXC headers in the TU, referencing the same conflicting type
  names DXC's own control exercises (`BYTE`, `BOOLEAN`, `BOOL`, `LONG`,
  `ULONG`, `LONGLONG`, `LONG_PTR`, `ULONG_PTR`, `ULONGLONG`, `GUID`,
  `REFGUID`). Compiles clean (exit 0). Capture:
  `manual-case-clang-control-directx-headers-only.txt`.
- Together these two controls prove the failure in `repro.cpp` is
  specifically the *coexistence* of both shims, not either shim being
  independently broken.
- An earlier control attempt also pulled in `<directx/d3d12shader.h>` in
  both `repro.cpp` and the DirectX-Headers-only control, matching the
  reporter's own include list more closely. That attempt failed with
  unrelated `unknown type name 'THIS'` / incomplete-type /
  `'virtual' can only appear on non-static member functions` errors in
  `d3d12shader.h`'s COM interface declarations -- neither shim defines the
  bare `THIS` COM-IDL macro that header needs (only `THIS_`), which is a
  pre-existing completeness gap in this exact combination of vendored
  headers, unrelated to the typedef conflict under test, and it fully
  masked the actual redefinition errors by hitting clang's error limit
  first. The reporter's own error transcript never mentions
  `d3d12shader.h` COM-interface errors either -- every line they quote is a
  typedef/`_GUID` redefinition -- so dropping `d3d12shader.h`/`<unknwn.h>`
  from repro.cpp and both controls is a closer match to the reported
  symptom, not a weaker one. See method-notes.md.

## Honest limitation of the local repro

The pinned DirectX-Headers submodule is at commit `980971e835876dc0cde415e8f9bc646e64667bf7`
(2022-01-31 upstream date; last touched in this repository by commit
`14a55b773` / PR #4810, 2022-11-23 -- confirmed via
`git log --all --reverse -- external/DirectX-Headers`, which shows that
commit both *introducing* and *pinning* the submodule, i.e. the pin has
never moved since the day the submodule was first added). At this pinned
commit, the Windows-type shim is still the single, pre-split file
`wsl/winadapter.h`; the reporter's DirectX-Headers release (v1.608.2) had
already split this into `wsl/stubs/basetsd.h` plus sibling stub headers.
This local repro therefore uses `wsl/winadapter.h`, not
`wsl/stubs/basetsd.h`, to exercise the same conflict.

This is not treated as a different defect: PR #8431's author (`amaiorano`,
2026-05-08T15:13:26Z) independently dug into exactly this question and
confirmed it in writing:

> In old DirectX-Headers: `wsl/stubs` really contains only stubs [...]
> `external/DirectX-Headers/include/wsl/winadapter.h` did contain Windows
> types for non-Windows, but this file was not included in DXC.
>
> In latest DirectX-Headers: `wsl/stubs` are no longer really stubs. Now
> `external/DirectX-Headers/include/wsl/stubs/rpcndr.h` defines
> `__CRT_UUID_DECL` and includes
> `external/DirectX-Headers/include/wsl/stubs/basetsd.h` (also in stubs)
> which is where most of what was in
> `external/DirectX-Headers/include/wsl/winadapter.h` has moved to.

i.e. the newer, split form is the *same content, relocated* -- confirming
the pinned submodule's pre-split shim is a faithful stand-in for the
reporter's post-split one, not an approximation of a different bug. The
same PR comment (2026-05-08T12:56:37Z) also independently lists the exact
underlying-type mismatches this session's repro reproduces:

> * The `BOOL` type going from `bool` to `uint32_t` might be a concern,
>   especially if used in the public facing API, but I'm not sure.
> * `BOOLEAN` was `char` and is now `BYTE` which is `unsigned char`
> * The rest went from non-sized types like `int`, `long`, `char`, to sized
>   types like `int32_t`, `int64_t`, `int8_t` [...]

which matches this session's own capture verbatim (`bool` vs `uint32_t`,
`long` vs `int32_t`, `unsigned long` vs `uint32_t`, and the `BOOLEAN`/`BYTE`
`char`-vs-`unsigned char` mismatch).

## History (no dxc.exe release bisect applies)

- **2018-06-17** (PR #1314, `git log --all -S"typedef unsigned char BYTE" -- "*WinAdapter.h"`
  followed with `--follow`/`--all` to survive the 2023-02-28 file move):
  DXC introduces its own non-Windows `WinAdapter.h` shim, including the
  `BYTE`/`BOOL`/`GUID`-family typedefs, for the original Linux port. Predates
  DirectX-Headers being vendored at all.
- **2022-11-23** (commit `14a55b773`, PR #4810 "[linux] Enable Reflection on
  *nix platforms"): DirectX-Headers is added as a submodule for the first
  time, pinned at upstream `980971e835876dc0cde415e8f9bc646e64667bf7`
  (2022-01-31). This is the moment the latent conflict enters the tree --
  both shims now coexist in the repository, though nothing in-tree combines
  them in one translation unit. Confirmed via
  `git log --all --reverse -- external/DirectX-Headers`: this is the
  *first* commit touching the path, and the pin has not moved since.
- **2023-03-04**: issue filed. The reporter's own project (not this
  repository's own CMake build) combines both header trees and hits the
  conflict.
- **2023-03-22 / 2024-03-14** (`LAKostis`): two follow-up comments asking
  for a DirectX-Headers submodule bump.
- **2024-08-27** (`damyanp`, maintainer): "we'll gladly consider a PR that
  fixes this, but we're not going to actively investigate this issue
  ourselves at this point."
- **2026-05-08** (PR #8431, `amaiorano`, "Update DirectX-Headers to latest",
  `Fixes #5079`): bumps the DirectX-Headers submodule and removes the
  now-duplicated types from `WinAdapter.h`. Raises the ABI concern (`BOOL`
  `bool`->`uint32_t`) and a packaging concern (GitHub-release consumers of
  `dxc/dxcapi.h`/`WinAdapter.h` as a standalone installed header would newly
  need DirectX-Headers on their own include path too).
- **2026-05-11**: last activity on PR #8431. Still **OPEN**, not draft,
  `MERGEABLE` (re-confirmed via `gh pr view 8431` during this session,
  "now" being 2026-08-19) -- no further comments in the ~3 months since,
  i.e. the maintainer/author design discussion has stalled without a
  decision, not been abandoned or superseded.
- **Today** (this session): submodule pin unchanged since 2022-11-23;
  conflict still fully reproducible in-tree with the exact vendored headers
  this repository ships (`manual-case-clang-conflict.txt`).

Every stable DXC release across this window ships the same from-scratch
`WinAdapter.h` design, so there is no release at which this stopped/started
reproducing on the DXC side -- the entire history is DirectX-Headers'
side (submodule pin) and PR #8431's stalled discussion, not a dxc.exe
regression window.

## Compiler Explorer

Skipped (`triage.py godbolt --issue 5079 --skip ...`). This is a C++
header/build-system conflict between two vendored header trees, not an
HLSL shader; there is no `.hlsl` for `dxc.exe` to compile and CE cannot host
a repro combining two arbitrary C++ header trees outside the `dxc` binary
itself. The local `clang` manual-case is the faithful, captured instrument
instead (see above).

## Labels

Current: `build`. Proposed addition: `linux` (label description: "Linux-
specific work") -- the conflict is specifically in the non-Windows/`_WIN32`-
undefined code path of both shims; nothing about it is Windows-specific.
`build` remains accurate and is left in place. No removal proposed.

## Suggested action

`needs-human-judgement`. The defect is real, faithfully reproduced, and
still present. It is not a case of "reopen a closed report" or "ask the
reporter for more info" -- a fix already exists as an open PR (#8431), but
its design raises a genuine, unresolved tradeoff (ABI-visible `BOOL` width
change; a new mandatory DirectX-Headers dependency for consumers of the
installed/released `dxc/dxcapi.h` + `WinAdapter.h`) that only a maintainer
can decide, not something a triage pass should resolve by picking a side.
